directAnswer: Xfinity cable and internet statements commonly add $35 to $58 per month in non-government company surcharges—including Broadcast TV Fees ($23.20–$28.00/mo), Regional Sports Network Fees ($12–$18/mo), and xFi Gateway rentals ($15/mo)—on top of base promotional rates. Buying a compatible DOCSIS 3.1 modem and requesting loyalty retention credits typically trims $360 to $650 annually.

fees.negotiable: Partial (Drop TV tier or request loyalty credit)
fees.howToChallenge: Not a government tax. Switching to internet-only or requesting a 12-month promotional loyalty credit eliminates or offsets it.
Applied automatically to Popular/Ultimate TV tiers even if you never watch sports. Ask to move to Choice TV or internet-only.
Return the xFi Gateway to an Xfinity Store with a receipt and activate an owned DOCSIS 3.1 modem (e.g., Arris S33 or Netgear CM2000).
Discretionary internal compliance fee rather than a statutory tax; cite the FCC Broadband Label total price when negotiating.

retentionScript: Hello, I am reviewing my Xfinity statement and noticed my rate jumped after my promotion expired, plus I am paying $39+ in Broadcast TV, Regional Sports, and xFi Gateway fees. Competitor fiber and 5G home internet plans in my ZIP code are advertising $50–$65 all-in. Please connect me with the Loyalty & Retention Department to match a current new-customer promotional rate or convert my account to internet-only using my own modem.
escalationChecklist: Check competing fiber/5G offers in your ZIP code (AT&T Fiber, Verizon 5G Home, T-Mobile Home Internet) before calling 1-800-934-6489.
Say 'Cancel Service' at the automated prompt to route directly to Xfinity Customer Retention specialists who hold promotional credit authority.
Return rented xFi equipment in person and keep the printed serial-number return receipt to stop recurring $15/mo charges.
If unauthorized add-ons or unnotified hikes remain unresolved after 14 days, file an informal FCC Consumer Billing Complaint and send a written notice.

faqs.question: Is the Xfinity Broadcast TV Fee a mandatory government tax?
faqs.answer: No. The Xfinity Broadcast TV Fee is a company-imposed surcharge used to offset local station retransmission costs. It is not collected by or remitted to any federal, state, or local tax authority.

faqs.question: How do I remove the $15 Xfinity xFi Gateway rental fee?
faqs.answer: Purchase an Xfinity-certified DOCSIS 3.1 modem, activate it in the Xfinity app, and return the rented gateway to an Xfinity retail store or UPS Store. Always keep the stamped serial-number return receipt.

faqs.question: What happens if Xfinity raises my bill when a 12-month promo ends?
faqs.answer: You are not locked into the higher post-promo rate unless bound by an active ETF term. Calling Retention and requesting a current 12-month or 24-month promotional rate—or switching to Xfinity NOW prepaid internet—typically lowers the monthly rate by $25 to $50.

faqs.question: Can I file an FCC complaint over undisclosed Xfinity surcharges?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under FCC Truth-in-Billing rules (47 C.F.R. § 64.2401), carriers must clearly distinguish company fees from government taxes and disclose rate increases. Filing an informal FCC complaint triggers a mandatory 30-day executive response from Comcast.

faqs.question: Is Verizon's Administrative & Telco Recovery Charge a government tax?
faqs.answer: No. Verizon classifies it under 'Verizon Surcharges' rather than 'Taxes, Governmental Surcharges & Fees.' It is a discretionary carrier fee used to offset cell-site leases and compliance costs.

faqs.question: How can I trigger a Verizon Wireless loyalty discount?
faqs.answer: Many postpaid customers receive a $10/line/month 12-month loyalty offer in the My Verizon app ('My Offers') shortly after generating a Number Transfer PIN or contacting Executive Retention.

faqs.question: Can I remove Verizon Mobile Protect after buying a new phone?
faqs.answer: Yes. Device protection is optional month-to-month coverage that can be canceled immediately in the My Verizon app without affecting your device financing or trade-in credits.

faqs.question: What if Verizon fails to apply my promised phone trade-in credit?
faqs.answer: Save your trade-in tracking number and submission ID, then submit a formal written billing notice referencing FCC Truth-in-Billing rules or escalate via the FCC Consumer Complaint Center.

fees.howToChallenge: Billed on all standard Spectrum TV bundles. Drop cable TV for an antenna or live streaming service to cut this surcharge immediately.
Spectrum's standalone DOCSIS modem is included at $0/mo, while the Wi-Fi router costs $7–$10/mo. Buy your own Wi-Fi 6 router ($60–$90) and return Spectrum's router.
Call Retention (request 'Cancel Service') and ask to be placed on Spectrum's current Life Unlimited / promotional 500 Mbps or 100 Mbps Advantage tier.

fees.typicalCost: Up to 1 full month upon cancellation
fees.howToChallenge: Spectrum does not prorate mid-cycle cancellations in most states. Always cancel 3–5 days before the end of your current billing cycle.

retentionScript: Hello, I saw my Spectrum statement increased to $XX.XX after my promotional discount stepped down. I see competing 5G home internet and fiber providers available at my address for $50 per month with no equipment fees. I would like to stay with Spectrum if Retention can match a $50–$60 promotional internet rate for 12 months and confirm my account is not being charged for a rented Wi-Fi router.

Call 1-833-267-6094 and state 'Cancel Service' to bypass frontline billing agents who cannot apply new-customer promotional codes.
Check if your household qualifies for Spectrum Internet Assist or Spectrum's 100 Mbps Advantage tier if you do not need gigabit speeds.
Confirm your billing cycle end date before cancelling any video add-on so you do not pay an unprorated extra month.

faqs.question: Does Spectrum charge for both a modem and a Wi-Fi router?
faqs.answer: No. Spectrum includes the standalone cable modem at $0/month, but charges $7 to $10 per month for its Wi-Fi router. Using your own Wi-Fi router eliminates that monthly fee completely.

faqs.question: Why does my Spectrum bill go up every 12 months?
faqs.answer: Spectrum structures most offers with 12-month or 24-month promotional discounts that step down in stages until reaching standard rack rates ($85–$100+ for internet alone). Calling Retention before or right after the step-down can reset your promo.

faqs.question: Will Spectrum prorate my final bill if I cancel mid-month?
faqs.answer: In most states (with specific exceptions such as New York and Maine), Spectrum bills full monthly subscription cycles without proration. Cancel 3 to 5 days prior to your cycle close date to avoid an extra month.

faqs.question: Can I remove Spectrum's Broadcast TV Surcharge while keeping cable?
faqs.answer: No—Spectrum applies the Broadcast TV Surcharge to all traditional TV packages carrying local broadcast channels. Dropping video to internet-only removes it entirely.

faqs.question: Can I cancel AT&T Next Up without paying off my phone?

faqs.question: Why did my AT&T Autopay discount decrease?

faqs.question: Is AT&T's $3.49 Administrative & Regulatory Cost Recovery Fee a tax?

faqs.question: How do I dispute an AT&T billing error if phone support refuses to credit it?
faqs.answer: Submit a written billing dispute referencing FCC Truth-in-Billing (47 C.F.R. § 64.2401) and file an informal complaint with the FCC, which routes directly to AT&T's Office of the President.

metaDescription: Audit hospital bills for Revenue Code 0450 ER facility fees, G0463 clinic fees, and unbundled supplies. Request an itemized UB-04 ledger free.
h1: Hospital Facility Fee (Revenue Code 0450) Auditor & Dispute Guide
directAnswer: Revenue Code 0450 (Emergency Room Facility Fee) and HCPCS G0463 (Hospital Outpatient Clinic Facility Fee) add $300 to $3,500+ in hospital overhead on top of your doctor's separate professional bill. Requesting an itemized UB-04/CPT statement, challenging upcoded ER acuity levels (CPT 99284/99285), and applying under IRC § 501(r) financial assistance regularly slashes balances by 40% to 100%.

Itemized Hospital Statement - Patient Account #MG-99214-B
- Revenue Code 0450: Emergency Room Facility Fee Level 4: $1,850.00
- CPT 99284: Emergency Dept Physician Evaluation: $950.00

- Revenue Code 0250: Pharmacy IV Saline 1000ml: $180.00
- Administrative Record Prep Surcharge: $120.00
Total Billed to Patient: $3,420.00

fees.negotiable: Auditable for Level Upcoding & Out-of-Network Caps
fees.statuteOrRule: No Surprises Act (42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111) & CMS ER Coding Guidelines
fees.howToChallenge: Request the hospital's internal ER acuity scoring matrix to verify whether a Level 4/5 (99284/99285) facility fee met medical complexity criteria.

fees.feeName: HCPCS G0463 / Rev Code 0510 (Outpatient Clinic Facility Fee)
fees.statuteOrRule: State Facility Fee Disclosure Laws & CMS Site-Neutral Rules
fees.howToChallenge: Hospitals acquiring doctor offices tack on outpatient facility fees; multiple states require advance written notice before billing facility fees at off-campus clinics.

fees.statuteOrRule: CMS NCCI Edits (National Correct Coding Initiative)
fees.howToChallenge: Routine supplies (gauze, basic saline, gloves) are generally encapsulated inside the facility fee. Demand an itemized audit against NCCI bundling edits.
Nonprofit hospitals cannot charge Financial Assistance-eligible patients more than Amounts Generally Billed (AGB) to insured patients.

retentionScript: Hello, I am calling regarding Patient Account #[Account #]. Before I make any payment, I am requesting a complete itemized billing statement with all CPT, HCPCS, and Revenue Codes—specifically the documentation supporting the Level 4/5 Revenue Code 0450 facility fee. Please also place a 30-day billing audit hold on this account and send me a copy of your hospital's IRC § 501(r) Financial Assistance Policy application.
escalationChecklist: Never pay a summary statement. Demand a full itemized bill listing every 5-digit CPT/HCPCS code and 4-digit Revenue Code.
Compare the hospital's billed CPT codes against your insurer's Explanation of Benefits (EOB) and FAIR Health / Medicare benchmark prices.
If the hospital is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (roughly 60% of U.S. hospitals), apply for Financial Assistance / Charity Care under IRC § 501(r).
Send a certified written itemized bill and coding audit request to pause collection escalation while the coding review is pending.

faqs.question: What is Revenue Code 0450 on a hospital bill?
faqs.answer: Revenue Code 0450 is the standard UB-04 billing code for Emergency Room facility overhead—covering nursing staff, building overhead, and equipment—billed separately from the ER physician's professional fee.

faqs.question: Why did I receive two bills for one emergency room visit?
faqs.answer: U.S. hospitals split billing into a 'facility claim' (UB-04 form from the hospital using Revenue Code 0450) and a 'professional claim' (CMS-1500 form from the ER physician, radiologist, or anesthesiologist).

faqs.question: Can I dispute an ER facility fee if I only received minor care?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ask the hospital billing department for a Coding Level Review to verify whether your visit met the clinical criteria for the billed CPT acuity level (e.g., 99284/99285 vs. lower-cost 99282/99283).

faqs.question: Does IRC § 501(r) apply to hospital facility fees?
faqs.answer: Yes. If the hospital is a tax-exempt nonprofit, its Financial Assistance Policy under 26 U.S.C. § 501(r) must cover emergency and medically necessary care—including hospital facility fees—and restrict extraordinary collection actions for at least 120 days.

seoTitle: ER Surprise Medical Bill Auditor (No Surprises Act) | ItsMyBill
metaDescription: Audit surprise out-of-network ER, anesthesia, radiology, or air ambulance bills under the federal No Surprises Act (42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111).
h1: ER Surprise Medical Bill Auditor (Federal No Surprises Act)
directAnswer: Under the federal No Surprises Act (42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111; 45 C.F.R. § 149), out-of-network emergency rooms, ER physicians, anesthesiologists, radiologists at in-network hospitals, and air ambulances cannot balance bill insured patients above their standard in-network copay, coinsurance, or deductible. Self-pay patients also have the right to a Good Faith Estimate and dispute bills exceeding it by $400 or more.
sampleBillText:
Out-of-Network Emergency Provider Statement
- CPT 99285: Emergency Dept Visit High Complexity (Out-of-Network): $2,100.00
- CPT 00840: Out-of-Network Anesthesiology Services (In-Network Hospital): $1,650.00
- CPT 74177: Out-of-Network Radiology CT Read: $1,100.00
Insurance Allowed: $1,200.00 | Balance Billed to Patient: $3,650.00

fees.howToChallenge: Emergency services must be processed at in-network cost-sharing without prior authorization; providers must resolve payment disputes with insurers via Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR).

fees.negotiable: Prohibited Without Valid Notice & Consent (Cannot Be Waived for Ancillary)
fees.howToChallenge: Anesthesiologists, radiologists, pathologists, and assistant surgeons at in-network facilities are prohibited from even asking you to sign a surprise-billing consent waiver.

fees.feeName: Self-Pay Bill Exceeding Good Faith Estimate by $400+
fees.howToChallenge: Uninsured or self-pay patients billed $400+ above their written Good Faith Estimate can initiate federal PPDR within 120 calendar days of receiving the bill.
Air ambulance balance billing is federally prohibited for insured patients (note: ground ambulances remain governed by state law rather than federal NSA).

retentionScript: Hello, I received an out-of-network balance bill for emergency care / ancillary services provided at an in-network hospital on [Date]. Under the federal No Surprises Act (42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111), my financial responsibility is strictly capped at my in-network cost-sharing amount. Please reprocess this claim with my health plan through the federal IDR pathway, remove the balance bill from my account, and pause all collections immediately.
escalationChecklist: Verify whether the care was emergency treatment OR an out-of-network clinician at an in-network hospital/ambulatory surgical center.
Call your health insurer first and confirm the claim was processed under the Qualifying Payment Amount (QPA) in-network cost-sharing rules.
Send our certified No Surprises Act Dispute Letter to the provider's billing department with your EOB attached.
If the provider refuses to withdraw the balance bill, file an official complaint with the CMS No Surprises Help Desk at 1-800-985-3059 or cms.gov/nosurprises.

faqs.question: Does the No Surprises Act cover out-of-network ER doctors?
faqs.answer: Yes. Even if the hospital itself is in-network (or out-of-network), emergency services—including ER physicians and post-stabilization care—cannot be balance billed above your in-network cost-sharing.

faqs.question: Does the No Surprises Act cover ground ambulances?
faqs.answer: No. The federal No Surprises Act covers air ambulances but currently excludes ground ambulances. However, more than a dozen states have enacted state-level ground ambulance balance-billing protections.

faqs.question: Can an anesthesiologist ask me to waive my No Surprises Act rights?
faqs.answer: No. Federal regulations (45 C.F.R. § 149.420) prohibit providers of ancillary services—including anesthesiology, radiology, pathology, neonatology, and hospitalists—from asking patients to sign notice-and-consent waivers.

faqs.question: Where do I report a hospital that violates the No Surprises Act?
faqs.answer: You can file a formal federal complaint directly with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) at cms.gov/nosurprises or by calling the No Surprises Help Desk at 1-800-985-3059.

faqs.question: How do I restore my T-Mobile $5/line AutoPay discount?
faqs.answer: Update your AutoPay payment method from a credit card to a bank checking account or debit card inside the T-Life app.

faqs.question: Can I cancel T-Mobile Protection<360> without affecting my phone promo credits?

faqs.question: What if T-Mobile raised the price of a plan I believed had a Price Lock?

faqs.question: Can I use my own modem with Cox Internet?

faqs.question: What is the Cox 40% retention discount tactic?

faqs.question: Does Cox charge a fee to cancel early?

faqs.question: Why does Frontier charge an Internet Infrastructure Surcharge?

faqs.question: Why did my Duke Energy bill jump even though my thermostat stayed the same?
faqs.answer: Three common triggers are: (1) a longer 33–35 day billing cycle, (2) semi-annual PUC-approved Fuel Cost Recovery or Storm Securitization rider updates, or (3) auxiliary electric heat strips running during cold snaps.

faqs.question: Can I request a free meter accuracy test from Duke Energy?

faqs.question: Does the FCC regulate Duke Energy electric bills?

faqs.question: Are optional surge protection plans on Duke Energy bills required?

directAnswer: PG&E residential electricity rates average over 38¢–52¢/kWh during 4 PM–9 PM peak hours on E-TOU-C plans, making California utility bills among the highest in the continental U.S. Auditing your PG&E rate plan (E-TOU-C vs. E-TOU-D vs. EV2-A), checking Medical Baseline or CARE/FERA discounts (18%–35% off), and verifying CCA generation credits can save $300 to $1,200+ annually.

escalationChecklist: Log into pge.com -> Rate Plan Comparison to test E-TOU-C vs. E-TOU-D vs. Tiered E-1 against your past 12 months of actual hourly usage.
Check income thresholds for CARE (30–35% off) and FERA (18% off for 3+ person households) and Medical Baseline eligibility.
Confirm your PG&E 'Generation Credit' properly offsets any Community Choice Aggregator (e.g., MCE, CleanPowerSF, EBCE, SJCE) line item.
For unresolved meter-accuracy disputes or billing errors, file an informal or formal complaint with the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) Consumer Affairs Branch.

faqs.question: Why does my PG&E bill show both PG&E Delivery and a Community Choice Aggregator (CCA) charge?
faqs.answer: You are not being double-billed for electricity—PG&E owns the wires (Delivery) while your local CCA buys the power (Generation), and PG&E deducts a 'Generation Credit' from its portion. Always verify the Generation Credit appears on page 3 of your statement.

faqs.question: How do I know if E-TOU-C or E-TOU-D is cheaper on PG&E?
faqs.answer: E-TOU-C gives a baseline credit but charges peak rates 4 PM–9 PM seven days a week. E-TOU-D has no baseline credit, but peak hours apply only 5 PM–8 PM on weekdays (weekends are 100% off-peak). Higher-usage homes often save on E-TOU-D.

faqs.question: What is the PG&E Medical Baseline Allowance?
faqs.answer: If anyone in your home relies on qualifying medical devices (such as a CPAP, oxygen concentrator, or temperature-sensitive medical condition), PG&E expands your lowest-cost Tier 1 allotment by 500 kWh/month or 25 therms/month.

faqs.question: Where do I file an official billing complaint against PG&E?
faqs.answer: After contacting PG&E billing, unresolved meter, tariff, or disconnection disputes can be escalated directly to the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) Consumer Affairs Branch at cpuc.ca.gov.
